_about: What each skill does in THIS game, for the hover on a skill's name in the character
creator and the level-up rank picker (the owner, 2026-10-06). Read by
book: one line of what the Core Rulebook says the skill is, paraphrased.
uses: what the engine and the GM actually do with it. Each names the file that does it
and a literal piece of that file (`find`); tests/test_skill_help.py reads every one
back, so a sentence here fails the suite the day its code moves or goes, instead of
lying on the page. The page is sent the words only, never the anchors.
not_yet: what the book offers that this game does not do yet, said plainly rather than
left for the player to assume. not_yet_uses names those uses by id (skill.<skill>.<use>);
tests/test_skill_uses.py fails when one is a row of content/rules/skill-uses.json, the
table of the uses the engine resolves, and a use whose `use` names a row says that row.
Mapped 2026-10-06 by grepping rules/, gm/, play/ and content/ for every skill id. A
skill that only appears as a bonus on gear, herbs or spells has no `uses`: a bonus to a
roll nothing makes is not a use. Modifier sources are the sheet's job (its Skills card
general: Any skill can also be called for by the GM when you try something it covers: the engine rolls d20 plus your bonus against a difficulty.

Still usable while raging, when most Dexterity skills are not.

handle animal.name: Handle Animal
handle animal.book: Make an animal do as you ask, teach it tricks, and train it for a purpose.

uses.text: Animals do not understand words. Speaking to one reaches nothing unless magic lets you speak with animals: this skill is how you get one to act.
Handle: DC 10 to have an animal do a trick it knows, a move action (+2 if it is hurt, +5 for a creature that is not an animal). Your own animal companion: a free action and +4.
Push: DC 25 to have it do something it does not know, a full-round action (a move action for your own companion).
Teach a trick: a week of lessons, three hours a day, at the trick's DC (15 or 20). An animal of Intelligence 1 learns three tricks at most, of 2, six. It waits In progress.
Train for a purpose: riding, combat riding, fighting, guarding, heavy labor, hunting or performance, two to six weeks. A mount trained for combat riding needs no Ride check to control it in a fight.
Rear a wild animal: DC 15 + its Hit Dice and a year, and never tried twice. In this game the animal must be at least indifferent and travel with you, as the world has no young to raise.

Wild empathy (druid, ranger): d20 + your level + Charisma to improve an animal's attitude as Diplomacy does a person's, within 30 feet, in a minute. A magical beast of an animal's wits is at -4. Diplomacy cannot reach an animal.

survival.name: Survival
survival.book: Live off the land, follow tracks, keep from getting lost, and read the weather.

uses.text: Foraging: each hour is a Survival check against the land's difficulty, with your Herbalist level added. The better the roll, the more you find.
Every crafter's gathering trip (prospecting for ore, quarrying salts, gathering for any craft) is the same Survival roll each hour, with that craft's level added.
Say you track someone or follow a trail, and the engine rolls Survival.
Living off the land: DC 10 to feed and water yourself for a day in the wild, and one more person for every 2 you beat it by.
uses.find: def _op_live_off_land(self, intent: Intent, partial: dict) -> Outcome:

survival.not_yet: Getting lost and reading the weather are not rolled. Hunger and thirst are Constitution rolls.

swim.name: Swim
swim.book: Swim, and keep your head above rough water.

uses.text: Say you swim, and the engine rolls Swim.
In the water every round: DC 10 calm, 15 rough, 20 stormy. Miss by up to 4 and you make no headway; by 5 or more and you go under.

use magic device.name: Use Magic Device
use magic device.book: Make a wand, scroll or magic item work for you when it was not made for your kind.

uses.text: Read a scroll or set off a wand your class does not cast: DC 20 + the scroll's caster level, or DC 20 for a wand. A second check emulates a scroll's ability score. A failure spends nothing; a natural 1 that fails locks you out for a day.

use magic device.not_yet: Activating an item blind, emulating a race or an alignment, and deciphering a written spell are not built: the circle's Identify reads a found scroll instead.
